vulnerability.category_l2: argument injection: a recipient address beginning with "-" is passed as a sendmail command-line option because the recipient list is not preceded by "--"

critical_operation.description: In -t mode, doSend() assembles the sendmail command line. It strips " -t" when envelope recipients are present, appends the sender as "-f" plus a shell-escaped address, and then appends each recipient as " " plus escapeshellarg(address) without a "--" end-of-options separator. escapeshellarg neutralizes shell metacharacters, but the sendmail process still parses each resulting argv token; a recipient such as "-X/tmp/out" or "-OQueueDirectory=..." is therefore consumed as an option rather than as an address. The 5.4.52 fix appends " --" before the recipient list so all following tokens are treated as operands.

entry_point.description: An application configures a sendmail transport with the -t flag (for example a sendmail:// DSN or new SendmailTransport("/usr/sbin/sendmail -t")) and lets a user-influenced address reach the envelope recipients, for example a contact form that adds the submitter to Cc. Mime Address accepts a leading-dash local part, so the value survives into doSend().

trace.description: doSend() removes " -t" when recipients are present and builds the command line from the configured sendmail command
each recipient address is appended with escapeshellarg but with no preceding "--"
ProcessStream receives the command and executes it; sendmail parses a leading-dash token as an option

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on CWE-88, the missing "--" mechanism, the <5.4.52 range and the v5.4.52 release, and both the CNA record and the GHSA name the same fix commit c4514486 (no dead reference in this advisory). NVD has a Primary CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH metric and a Secondary CVSS 4.0 8.7 HIGH metric; both compute to High. The GHSA label MODERATE conflicts with both and is recorded as a defect. The commit subject claims addresses starting with a dash are rejected, but the diff only adds "--".

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read SendmailTransport::doSend at v5.4.45 and confirm recipients are appended without "--".
An independent reviewer must confirm c4514486 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that the diff only adds "--" despite the commit subject.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
An independent reviewer must assess whether the -t-mode narrative matches the code (the code strips " -t" when recipients exist) and record any discrepancy.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No sendmail binary, PHP runtime or message was executed; the finding is static and the option-parsing consequence is reasoned from sendmail semantics.
Exploitability requires the application to configure the -t mode and let a user-influenced address into the envelope recipients; no specific application was tested.

The advisory says "-t mode appends recipients to the command line", while the code removes " -t" when recipients are non-empty before appending them; the dossier describes the code path rather than repeating the advisory wording.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
GHSA label MODERATE disagrees with the 4.0 8.7 and 3.1 7.5 scores; the commit subject claims a dash rejection that the diff does not contain.
The GitHub advisory page and OSV publish CVSS 4.0 6.2 MODERATE with PR:L/VC:H, inconsistent with the CVE List v5 CNA metric (PR:N/VC:N, 8.7) issued by the same assigner.
open_questions: Which sendmail options are usable with the privileges of the web process was not assessed.
Whether the sendmail DSN commonly enables -t in real deployments was not surveyed.
